questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She _______ to be understood by the society.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She _______ to be understood by the society.
questions.solution: 'Sought' will be used because it means to attempt to gain or achieve something. The sentence mentions that she was trying to be understood by society, making 'sought' the most appropriate choice here. Whereas, 'Looked' means to see, 'Chased' means to pursue or try to catch something (but it doesn’t fit the context), and 'Hunted' means to search or hunt for something, which is not suitable in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher encouraged students to cultivate a __________ attitude towards learning, embracing challenges as opportunities for growth
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher encouraged students to cultivate a __________ attitude towards learning, embracing challenges as opportunities for growth
questions.solution: Resilient' will be used because it refers to the ability to recover quickly from difficulties or adapt to challenges. The sentence suggests that students are encouraged to embrace challenges as opportunities for growth, which aligns with the quality of being resilient. 'Redundant' means unnecessary or superfluous, which does not fit the context as it does not relate to embracing challenges or growth. 'Stagnant' refers to a lack of activity, growth, or progress, which is the opposite of what is encouraged in the sentence. 'Complacent' means being overly satisfied with oneself or one’s situation, often leading to a lack of effort, which also contradicts the idea of embracing challenges.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Parties were counselled (A) / to advice new (B) / entrants to (C) / refrain from heckling. (D)
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Parties were counselled (A) / to advice new (B) / entrants to (C) / refrain from heckling. (D)
questions.solution: 'advise' will be used instead of 'advice' because 'advice' is a noun and here a verb is required. 'Advise' is a verb that means to give suggestions; Like— The teacher advised the students to study regularly.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Just when they reach the airport, the flight had departed from the runway.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Just when they reach the airport, the flight had departed from the runway.

options.html: Just before they reached
after they just reach
Just when they have reached

questions.solution: 'Just before they reached' (Option B) will be used instead of 'Just when they reach' because the Principal Clause uses Past Perfect Tense ('had departed'), which makes it clear that the Subordinate Clause will use Past Simple Tense ('reached'). 'Just before' is a time-indicating word that is appropriate with Past Tense.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Thus, children in India have the unique opportunity to receive a world-class education. B. Since ancient times, India has been known for its great educational system. C. Today, there are thousands of schools in India, many of which are among the best in the world. D. The country's first university, Nalanda, was founded over 1,000 years ago.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Thus, children in India have the unique opportunity to receive a world-class education.

B. Since ancient times, India has been known for its great educational system.

C. Today, there are thousands of schools in India, many of which are among the best in the world.

D. The country's first university, Nalanda, was founded over 1,000 years ago.
questions.solution: B introduces the topic by stating that India has been known for its great educational system since ancient times. This is the most logical starting point as it sets the historical context.
